Seminar Title:

Studies on Glutathione Reductase from Brassica Juncea: Purification, Characterization and Functional Applications

Seminar Type:

Seminar Room, BM Dept.

Contact:

Nandini Sarkar

Abstract:

This study investigates the comparative effects of nickel and cobalt nanoparticles (NiNPs and CoNPs) on the physiological and biochemical responses of Brassica juncea. The increasing application and environmental accumulation of metal-based nanoparticles have raised concerns regarding their potential effects on plant growth, cellular metabolism, and oxidative stress responses. In the present study, B. juncea plants were exposed to different concentrations of NiNPs and CoNPs to evaluate their effects on plant growth, photosynthetic pigments, oxidative status, antioxidant defense, and protein profiles. The synthesized nanoparticles were characterized using Dynamic Light Scattering (DLS), zeta potential analysis, X-Ray Diffraction (XRD), UV&ndashVisible spectroscopy, Fourier-Transform Infrared Spectroscopy(FTIR).and Field Emission Scanning Electron Microscope (FESEM) to determine their physicochemical and structural properties.&nbspThe physiological effects of nanoparticle exposure were assessed by evaluating seed germination, root and shoot growth, and chlorophyll content. The generation of oxidative stress in response to NiNP and CoNP exposure was evaluated through the estimation of hydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂), an important indicator of reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation. The antioxidant defense response was investigated by determining the activities of major enzymatic antioxidants, including superoxide dismutase (SOD), catalase (CAT), peroxidase (POD), ascorbate peroxidase (APX), and glutathione reductase (GR). These enzymes collectively contribute to the detoxification of ROS and maintenance of cellular redox balance under stress conditions. Overall, this study demonstrates that NiNPs and CoNPs can significantly influence plant growth, photosynthetic pigments, oxidative status, antioxidant defense, and protein expression in B. juncea. The integrated assessment of physiological, biochemical, and protein-level responses provides a broader understanding of nanoparticle-induced stress in plants and highlights the coordinated role of antioxidant defense mechanisms in maintaining cellular homeostasis. The findings contribute to the understanding of plant responses to metal nanoparticles and provide useful insights into their potential biological and environmental impacts.
